1.1: After Ahab died, Moab got bold and stopped paying tribute to Israel. They was like, 'We out.'
1.2: Meanwhile, Ahaziah—Ahab's son—fell through the upstairs railing in Samaria and got hurt bad. So he sent some messengers out, like, 'Go ask Baal-Zebub, that god over in Ekron, if I'm gonna make it through this.'
1.3: But the angel of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite and told him, 'Ayo, get up and intercept them messengers from the king of Samaria. Tell 'em: "For real? Ain't no God in Israel? That's why y'all running to Baal-Zebub?"'
1.4: 'Well, here's the word from The Most High: You ain't getting up off that bed. You finna die right there.' Then Elijah just dipped.
1.5: The messengers turned right back around, and when they got to Ahaziah, he was like, 'Y'all back quick. What happened?'
1.6: They told him, 'Some dude ran up on us and said, "Turn back to the king and tell him: The Most High said, 'So you really out here acting like there ain't no God in Israel? That's why you asking Baal-Zebub? Welp, you ain't leaving that bed—you finna die.'"'
1.7: Ahaziah was like, 'Who? What this dude look like that told y'all this?'
1.8: They said, 'He was wild-looking, hairy, with a leather belt around his waist.' And the king was like, 'Ah, that's Elijah the Tishbite. I should've known.'
1.9: So the king sent a captain with fifty men to go get Elijah. They rolled up and found him chilling on top of a hill. The captain was like, 'Yo, man of God, the king said, "Come down from there!"'
1.10: Elijah hit 'em with, 'Oh, I'm a man of God? Aight. If that's true, then let fire come down from heaven and burn y'all up.' And boom—fire dropped from the sky and wiped them all out.
1.11: So the king sent another fifty soldiers with a captain. They came up and said, 'Man of God, the king said, "Come down here right now!"'
1.12: Elijah was like, 'Oh, I'm a man of God? Bet. If that's the case, let fire come down from heaven and burn y'all up too.' And once again—fire dropped and took 'em all out.
1.13: Then the king sent a third squad, but this captain was smarter. He walked up, dropped to his knees, and pleaded, 'Man of God, please, don't do us like the last two groups. We don't want no smoke—literally.'
1.14: 'Look, we already seen fire come down and take out the last two squads. But please, let us live, man. We just following orders.'
1.15: Then the angel of the Lord told Elijah, 'Go with him, don't trip. You good.' So Elijah got up and went with the captain to see the king.
1.16: When he got there, he told Ahaziah straight up, 'Look, The Most High said: "Since you decided to check in with Baal-Zebub instead of Me, you ain't getting up from that bed. You finna die."'
1.17: And just like that, Ahaziah died—exactly how The Most High said through Elijah. Since he ain't have no sons, his brother Jehoram took over in his place, in the second year of Jehoram, king of Judah.
1.18: Everything else Ahaziah did? If you wanna know, go check the official records—the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

2.1: When the Lord was 'bout to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha was walking from Gilgal.
2.2: Elijah told Elisha, 'Aye, stay here. The Lord told me to go to Bethel.' But Elisha wasn't having it. He said, 'Nah, as sure as the Lord lives and you alive, I ain't leaving you.' So they kept it moving to Bethel.
2.3: At Bethel, the prophets-in-training came up to Elisha and was like, 'Yo, you know the Lord taking your master away today, right?' Elisha was like, 'Yeah, I know. Chill with all that.'
2.4: Elijah told him again, 'Stay here, Elisha. The Lord told me to go to Jericho.' But Elisha said, 'Nah, I ain't leaving you.' So they went on to Jericho.
2.5: Then the prophets at Jericho pulled up on Elisha and told him the same thing, 'You know Elijah getting taken today, right?' And Elisha was like, 'Yeah, I know. Be quiet.'
2.6: Elijah told him one more time, 'Stay here, the Lord sent me to the Jordan.' But Elisha was locked in. He said, 'As long as the Lord lives and you alive, I ain't leaving you.' So they kept it pushing.
2.7: Fifty of the prophets stood at a distance, watching as Elijah and Elisha stood by the Jordan River.
2.8: Elijah took off his cloak, rolled it up, and smacked the water with it. The water split in two, and they walked across on dry ground.
2.9: After they got to the other side, Elijah turned to Elisha and said, 'Aight, what you want me to do for you before I get taken up?' Elisha said, 'Let me get a double portion of your spirit.'
2.10: Elijah was like, 'Man, you asking for a tough one. But if you see me when I go, then it's yours. If not, then nah.'
2.11: As they was walking and talking, outta nowhere, a chariot of fire with horses of fire pulled up, split them apart, and Elijah got swooped up to heaven in a whirlwind.
2.12: Elisha saw it and shouted, 'My father, my father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!' And just like that, Elijah was gone. Elisha tore his clothes in two out of grief.
2.13: Then he picked up Elijah's cloak that had fallen and walked back to the Jordan River.
2.14: He took the cloak, smacked the water, and said, 'Where's the Lord, the God of Elijah?' And boom—the water split just like before, and he walked across.
2.15: When the prophets from Jericho saw this, they was like, 'Yo, Elijah's spirit is on Elisha now.' They came up, bowed down, and showed respect.
2.16: The prophets told Elisha, 'Look, we got fifty strong men here. Let 'em go look for Elijah. Maybe the Lord picked him up and dropped him on a mountain or in a valley somewhere.' But Elisha was like, 'Nah, don't do that.'
2.17: They kept pressuring him 'til he got tired of hearing it and said, 'Fine, go ahead.' They sent the fifty men to search for three days, but they ain't find nothing.
2.18: When they came back, Elisha was still chilling in Jericho. He hit 'em with, 'I told y'all not to go, but y'all don't listen.'
2.19: Then the people of Jericho told Elisha, 'Look, the city's nice and all, but the water's bad and the land ain't producing crops.'
2.20: Elisha said, 'Bring me a new bowl with some salt in it.' So they did.
2.21: Then he went to the water source, threw the salt in, and said, 'The Lord says: I just healed this water—no more death or drought from it.'
2.22: And just like that, the water stayed clean from then on, just like Elisha said.
2.23: Elisha left Jericho and went to Bethel. While he was walking, some wild kids ran up on him, clowning him like, 'Go on up, baldy! Get up outta here, baldy!'
2.24: Elisha turned around, looked at them, and called down a curse in the name of the Lord. Next thing you know, two she-bears ran out the woods and tore up forty-two of them kids.
2.25: After that, Elisha went on to Mount Carmel, then back to Samaria.

3.1: Jehoram, Ahab's son, took over as king of Israel in Samaria during Jehoshaphat's 18th year ruling Judah. He held the throne for 12 years.
3.2: Now, he was on some evil stuff, but he wasn't as bad as his mama and daddy. At least he got rid of that Baal statue his father put up.
3.3: But don't get it twisted—he still kept up Jeroboam's mess, the same sins that had Israel out here wildin'. He ain't turn away from that.
3.4: Now, Mesha, the king of Moab, was in the sheep business. Every year, he had to pay the king of Israel 100,000 lambs and the wool from 100,000 rams.
3.5: But soon as Ahab died, Moab was like, 'Nah, we ain't doing that no more,' and they straight-up rebelled against Israel.
3.6: So Jehoram left Samaria and called up all Israel to get ready for war.
3.7: Then he hit up Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, like, 'Ayo, Moab trippin'. They rebelling against me. You riding with me or what?'
3.8: Jehoshaphat said, 'I got you. My people, your people. My horses, your horses. Which way we rolling up?'
3.9: Jehoram said, 'We going through the Wilderness of Edom.' So the kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom all linked up and started marching. But after seven days in the desert, they ran out of water for the army and their animals.
3.10: Jehoram panicked, 'Man, the Lord set us up! He brought all three of us kings out here just to hand us over to Moab!'
3.11: Jehoshaphat was like, 'Hold up, ain't no prophet of the Lord around? We need to check in with Him first.'
3.12: One of Jehoram's servants said, 'Yeah, Elisha, son of Shaphat, is here. He used to be Elijah's right-hand man.'
3.13: Jehoshaphat said, 'Say less. He got the word of the Lord.' So all three kings went to see Elisha.
3.14: Elisha looked at Jehoram and was like, 'Bruh, what you want with me? Go ask your daddy's prophets. Go ask your mama's prophets.'
3.15: Jehoram said, 'Nah, this serious. The Lord brought us here, and now it's looking like He 'bout to let Moab take us out.'
3.16: Elisha said, 'Listen, if it wasn't for King Jehoshaphat standing right here, I wouldn't even give you the time of day.'
3.17: 'But since he's here, get me a musician.' When the music started playing, the Spirit of the Lord came over Elisha.
3.18: Elisha said, 'Here's what the Lord says: Dig a bunch of ditches in this valley.'
3.19: 'You ain't gon' see no wind, no rain, but somehow, this valley gon' fill up with water. You, your army, and all your animals gon' drink plenty.'
3.20: 'And oh yeah, that's light work for the Lord. He also gon' hand Moab over to y'all.'
3.21: 'Y'all gon' run through their cities, take down all their good land, cut down all their trees, and clog up their wells with rocks. Ain't gon' be nothing left when y'all done.'
3.22: The next morning, right when the grain offering was being made, water came rushing in from Edom, flooding the land.
3.23: Meanwhile, the Moabites heard that the kings were rolling up on them, so every man old enough to hold a sword got posted up at the border.
3.24: When they woke up in the morning, the sun was shining on the water, making it look red like blood.
3.25: They said, 'Yo! Them kings must've turned on each other! They done wiped themselves out. Let's go take what's left!'
3.26: So they ran up to Israel's camp, thinking it was all good—until Israel popped out and ambushed them. The Moabites tried to run, but Israel chased them down, wiping them out.
3.27: They destroyed Moab's cities, threw rocks all over the land, clogged up all the wells, and cut down the trees. Only the stronghold at Kir Haraseth was left standing, but even that got surrounded and attacked.
3.28: When the king of Moab saw that he was getting worked, he took 700 of his best soldiers and tried to break through to the king of Edom. But they couldn't.
3.29: In a desperate move, he sacrificed his own firstborn son—the one who was supposed to be king after him—right there on the wall.
3.30: That move sent shockwaves through Israel, and they was like, 'Yeah… we out.' So they packed up and went back home.

4.1: One day, a widow of one of the prophets' followers ran up on Elisha crying. She said, 'My husband—your servant—died, and you know he was a God-fearing man. But now, the bill collectors coming to take my two sons as slaves to pay off the debt.'
4.2: Elisha said, 'What you want me to do? Tell me, what you got in your house?' She said, 'I got nothing but this little jar of oil.'
4.3: Elisha said, 'Aight, go borrow as many empty jars as you can from your neighbors—don't hold back, get a whole lot of 'em.'
4.4: 'Then go in the house with your sons, shut the door, and start pouring that oil into the jars. When one fills up, set it to the side.'
4.5: She did exactly what he said—shut the door, and her sons kept bringing jars while she kept pouring.
4.6: When all the jars were full, she told her son, 'Bring me another one.' But he said, 'That's it, we out of jars.' And just like that, the oil stopped flowing.
4.7: She ran back to Elisha and told him what happened. He said, 'Now go sell all that oil, pay your debt, and live off the rest with your sons.'
4.8: One day, Elisha was in Shunem, where a well-off woman lived. She saw him passing through and insisted he stop by for a meal. From then on, every time he was in town, he ate at her place.
4.9: She told her husband, 'Babe, I'm telling you, this man is holy. He's always coming through here.'
4.10: 'Let's build him a little room upstairs—put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp in there—so whenever he comes by, he got somewhere to stay.'
4.11: One day, Elisha was chilling in that room, lying down, and he called his servant Gehazi.
4.12: He told Gehazi, 'Go get that Shunammite woman.' She came and stood before him.
4.13: Elisha told Gehazi, 'Tell her, "Look, you've done all this for us. What can we do for you? You want me to put in a good word with the king or the army commander?"'
4.14: But she said, 'I'm good, I got everything I need among my people.'
4.15: Elisha turned to Gehazi, 'So what can we do for her?' Gehazi said, 'Well, she don't got no kids, and her husband is old.'
4.16: Elisha said, 'Call her back.' She came and stood in the doorway. Elisha said, 'This time next year, you gonna be holding a son.'
4.17: She said, 'No, man of God, don't play with me like that.' But sure enough, she got pregnant and had a son just like Elisha said.
4.18: The boy grew up, and one day he went out to his dad in the field with the workers.
4.19: He started crying, 'My head! My head!' His dad told a servant, 'Take him to his mama.'
4.20: The servant carried the boy home to his mother. He sat in her lap till noon, then he died.
4.21: She took him upstairs, laid him on Elisha's bed, shut the door, and left.
4.22: She called her husband and said, 'Send me a servant and a donkey. I need to go see the man of God real quick.'
4.23: Her husband said, 'Why today? It ain't the Sabbath or a festival.' She just said, 'It's all good.'
4.24: She saddled the donkey and told the servant, 'Let's ride. Don't slow down unless I say so.'
4.25: She pulled up to Mount Carmel, where Elisha was. When Elisha saw her coming, he told Gehazi, 'Look, the Shunammite woman coming!'
4.26: 'Run over and ask her if she, her husband, and her son are good.' She said, 'We good.'
4.27: But when she got to Elisha, she grabbed his feet. Gehazi tried to push her off, but Elisha said, 'Chill, she's deeply troubled. The Lord ain't showed me what's wrong yet.'
4.28: She said, 'Did I ask for a son? Didn't I tell you not to get my hopes up?'
4.29: Elisha told Gehazi, 'Get ready, take my staff, and go. If you see anybody, don't stop to talk—just go lay my staff on the boy.'
4.30: But the boy's mama said, 'I ain't leaving unless you come too.' So Elisha went with her.
4.31: Gehazi got there first, laid the staff on the boy, but nothing happened. He ran back and told Elisha, 'He's still dead.'
4.32: When Elisha got to the house, the boy was lying there, dead.
4.33: Elisha shut the door, just him and the boy, and prayed to the Lord.
4.34: He stretched out over the boy—mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, hands to hands. The boy's body started warming up.
4.35: Elisha got up, paced around, then stretched out over him again. Suddenly, the boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
4.36: Elisha told Gehazi, 'Call his mama.' She came in, and Elisha said, 'Pick up your son.'
4.37: She fell at his feet, bowed in thanks, then scooped up her son and left.
4.38: Elisha went back to Gilgal, and there was a famine in the land. The prophets-in-training were sitting around, and Elisha told his servant, 'Put on a big pot and make some stew.'
4.39: One of them went out to pick herbs, but he grabbed some wild gourds too. He didn't know what they were, but he cut them up and threw them in the stew.
4.40: When they started eating, they panicked, 'Man of God, there's poison in this pot! We can't eat this!'
4.41: Elisha said, 'Bring me some flour.' He threw it in the pot and said, 'Now serve it.' And just like that, the stew was good to eat.
4.42: One day, a man from Baal Shalisha brought Elisha twenty loaves of barley bread and fresh grain.
4.43: Elisha told his servant, 'Feed it to the people.' The servant said, 'What? This little bit for 100 men?'
4.44: Elisha said, 'Do it. The Lord says they'll eat and have leftovers.' And sure enough, they all ate, and there was some left.

5.1: Naaman was that dude—commander of the Syrian army, respected by his king 'cause the Lord had given him big wins. He was a real warrior, but he had leprosy.
5.2: One time, the Syrians raided Israel and snatched up a young girl. She ended up working for Naaman's wife.
5.3: One day, she told her mistress, 'Man, if only my master could go see the prophet in Samaria, he'd get healed for sure!'
5.4: Naaman went straight to the king and told him what the girl said.
5.5: The king of Syria said, 'Aight, go ahead. I'll send a letter to the king of Israel for you.' So Naaman took off, bringing ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten fresh outfits.
5.6: When he got to the king of Israel, he handed him the letter, which said, 'I'm sending my guy Naaman to you. Heal him of his leprosy.'
5.7: When the king of Israel read that, he tore his clothes, like, 'What kinda setup is this?! You think I'm God? I can't heal nobody! This man tryna start beef with me!'
5.8: Elisha heard the king was stressing and sent a message: 'Why you tearing your clothes? Send him my way. He gon' learn today that there's a real prophet in Israel.'
5.9: So Naaman rolled up to Elisha's crib with his whole squad—horses, chariots, everything.
5.10: But instead of coming out, Elisha sent a messenger: 'Go wash yourself in the Jordan River seven times. Your skin gon' be brand new.'
5.11: Naaman got mad. 'Hold up, I thought this prophet was gon' come out, call on the Lord, wave his hand over me, and boom—I'm healed!'
5.12: 'Ain't the rivers in Damascus better than this dirty Jordan River? I coulda washed at home!' So he stormed off, big mad.
5.13: But his servants stepped in like, 'Boss, if he told you to do something difficult, you woulda done it, right? This is easy—just wash and be clean.'
5.14: Naaman thought about it, went down to the Jordan, dipped in seven times just like Elisha said—and boom! His skin was smooth like a newborn baby.
5.15: He went back to Elisha with his crew, stood before him, and said, 'Now I know—ain't no other God in the whole world except in Israel. Please take this gift from me.'
5.16: But Elisha said, 'Nah, as surely as the Lord lives, I ain't taking nothing.' And no matter how much Naaman insisted, Elisha wasn't budging.
5.17: So Naaman said, 'Alright then, can I at least take some dirt back with me? From now on, I ain't worshiping no other gods, only the Lord.'
5.18: 'But one thing—when my king takes me to the temple of Rimmon and I gotta bow with him, I hope the Lord understands.'
5.19: Elisha said, 'Go in peace.' So Naaman headed out.
5.20: Now Gehazi, Elisha's servant, was watching all this go down and was thinking, 'Man, my master just let this Syrian slide without taking anything? Nope, I'm about to go get me something.'
5.21: So Gehazi ran after Naaman. When Naaman saw him coming, he got down from his chariot and said, 'Everything good?'
5.22: Gehazi said, 'Yeah, yeah, all good. My master just sent me to tell you that two young prophets just showed up from the hills of Ephraim. Can you hook 'em up with a talent of silver and two fresh outfits?'
5.23: Naaman said, 'Take two talents!' He even had two of his guys carry the silver and clothes ahead for Gehazi.
5.24: When they got to Gehazi's spot, he took the stuff, hid it in his house, and sent the men away.
5.25: Then he went back to Elisha like nothing happened. Elisha said, 'Where you been, Gehazi?' Gehazi said, 'Nowhere, I ain't go nowhere.'
5.26: Elisha looked at him, 'Bruh, you think I ain't see you when Naaman hopped off his chariot to meet you? You really think this was the time to be out here collecting money and clothes, talking about buying olive groves, vineyards, sheep, cattle, and servants?'
5.27: 'Since you wanted to chase that money, Naaman's leprosy finna stick to you and your family forever.' And just like that, Gehazi walked out of there looking white as snow—leprosy all over him.

6.1: The prophets-in-training came to Elisha like, 'Yo, this spot we staying in? It's way too small.'
6.2: 'Let's go to the Jordan, everybody grab some wood, and we'll build a bigger place.'
6.3: One of them said, 'Elisha, you rolling with us?'
6.4: Elisha said, 'Yeah, I got y'all.' So they all headed to the Jordan and started chopping trees.
6.5: But while one of them was chopping, the ax head flew off and fell into the river. He panicked, 'Oh no! That wasn't even mine—I borrowed it!'
6.6: Elisha said, 'Where it drop at?' The guy pointed, so Elisha cut a stick, threw it in the water, and—boom—the iron ax head floated up.
6.7: 'Go ahead, grab it,' Elisha said. The guy reached in and pulled it out.
6.8: Meanwhile, the king of Syria was plotting war against Israel. He told his crew, 'We setting up camp right here.'
6.9: But Elisha got a message from God and told the king of Israel, 'Don't go near that spot—the Syrians waiting on you there.'
6.10: So Israel's king listened and dodged the trap. And this didn't happen just once or twice—it kept happening.
6.11: The king of Syria got fed up. He called his men, 'Aight, who snitching? Which one of y'all working for Israel?'
6.12: One of his servants said, 'Ain't nobody snitching, my king. It's that prophet Elisha—he be knowing everything, even what you say in your bedroom.'
6.13: The king said, 'Find out where he at. I'm sending troops to grab him.' Somebody came back saying, 'He in Dothan.'
6.14: So the king sent horses, chariots, and a whole army. They pulled up at night and surrounded the city.
6.15: Elisha's servant woke up, stepped outside, and saw the army everywhere. He ran back in like, 'Master! What we gon' do?!'
6.16: Elisha said, 'Chill, don't be scared. We got more on our side than they got on theirs.'
6.17: Then Elisha prayed, 'Lord, open his eyes so he can really see.' The Lord did, and the servant saw chariots of fire and heavenly warriors all over the mountain, surrounding Elisha.
6.18: When the Syrian army started closing in, Elisha prayed again, 'Lord, hit 'em with blindness.' And just like that, they all went blind.
6.19: Elisha walked up to them like, 'Y'all in the wrong spot. Lemme take y'all to the man you looking for.' Then he led them straight to Samaria.
6.20: When they got there, Elisha prayed, 'Lord, open their eyes now.' They looked around and realized—uh oh—they were right in the middle of Israel's territory.
6.21: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, 'Should I kill 'em? Say the word, I'll take 'em out!'
6.22: Elisha said, 'Nah, we don't do prisoners like that. Feed 'em, give 'em water, then send 'em back home.'
6.23: So the king made a big feast for them. After they ate and drank, they went back to Syria, and after that, the Syrian raiders stopped messing with Israel.
6.24: Later on, King Ben-Hadad of Syria got his whole army together and laid siege to Samaria, cutting off supplies.
6.25: It got so bad that a donkey's head was selling for eighty silver coins, and people were even buying bird poop for food.
6.26: One day, as the king of Israel was walking on the city wall, a woman yelled, 'Help me, my lord, O king!'
6.27: He said, 'If the Lord ain't helping you, how am I supposed to? Ain't no food in the fields or the vineyards.'
6.28: 'What's wrong?' he asked. She said, 'This woman told me, "Let's eat your son today, and we'll eat mine tomorrow."'
6.29: 'So yesterday, we cooked my son and ate him. But today, when I told her it was her turn, she went and hid her son!'
6.30: When the king heard that, he tore his clothes in grief. As he walked along the wall, people saw that under his robe, he was wearing sackcloth—showing how bad things had gotten.
6.31: The king got mad and said, 'May God do worse to me if Elisha still got his head by the end of today!'
6.32: Elisha was chilling at home with some elders when he said, 'Look, the king's son of a murderer just sent somebody to kill me. When he gets here, shut the door. His master gon' be right behind him.'
6.33: Right as he finished talking, the king's messenger showed up, and the king himself came in after him. He said, 'This disaster came straight from the Lord—why should I wait on Him any longer?'

7.1: Elisha said, 'Listen up, this what the Lord says: By this time tomorrow, you gon' be able to buy fine flour and barley dirt cheap right at the city gate in Samaria.'
7.2: One of the king's officers, who was leaning on him, scoffed and said, 'Man, even if the Lord opened up windows in heaven, that couldn't happen!' Elisha looked at him and said, 'Oh, you gon' see it with your own eyes—but you ain't gon' get to eat none of it.'
7.3: Now outside the city gate, there were four men with leprosy. They looked at each other and said, 'Bruh, why we just sitting here waiting to die?'
7.4: 'If we go in the city, we starve. If we stay here, we starve. Might as well roll up to the Syrian camp and surrender. If they let us live, cool. If they kill us, we was gon' die anyway.'
7.5: So at twilight, they got up and walked to the Syrian camp. But when they got there—nobody was there.
7.6: See, the Lord had made the Syrians hear what sounded like a whole army—chariots, horses, and soldiers. They got scared and said, 'Yo, Israel must've hired the Hittites and Egyptians to ambush us!'
7.7: So they panicked and ran for their lives, leaving everything—tents, horses, donkeys—all still set up.
7.8: When the lepers got to the camp, they went inside one tent, ate good, drank up, grabbed some silver, gold, and clothes, then went and hid it. Then they hit another tent and did the same.
7.9: But then they was like, 'Yo, we wrong for this. This is good news, and we just keeping it to ourselves? If we wait till morning, we might get in trouble. Let's go tell the king's people now.'
7.10: So they ran back to the city, told the gatekeepers, 'We went to the Syrian camp—nobody there! Just horses, donkeys, and all their tents left behind!'
7.11: The gatekeepers spread the word, and soon the whole palace knew.
7.12: But the king was suspicious. He said, 'I bet this a trap. They know we starving, so they hiding, waiting for us to come out so they can rush in and take the city.'
7.13: One of his officers said, 'Look, let's send some men with a few horses to check it out. Worst case, they die like the rest of us starving in here, but at least we'll know what's up.'
7.14: So they took two chariots with horses and sent them out toward the Syrian camp.
7.15: They followed the trail all the way to the Jordan River. The road was littered with clothes and weapons the Syrians had dropped while running for their lives. So they went back and told the king.
7.16: Then everybody in the city rushed out and looted the Syrian camp. And just like Elisha said, flour and barley was selling for cheap at the gate.
7.17: Now remember that officer who doubted Elisha? The king had put him in charge of the city gate, but when the people rushed out, they trampled him to death.
7.18: So just like Elisha had prophesied, the food was sold for the price he said.
7.19: And just like Elisha told that officer—'You gon' see it, but you ain't gon' eat none of it'—
7.20: That's exactly what happened. He saw it with his own eyes, but the people ran him over at the gate, and he died.

8.1: Elisha told the woman whose son he had brought back to life, 'Look, you and your family need to pack up and leave. The Lord about to send a famine on this land for seven years.'
8.2: So she listened to the man of God, took her people, and went to live in Philistine territory for those seven years.
8.3: After the seven years were up, she came back to Israel and went to the king to ask for her house and land back.
8.4: Now at the same time, the king was talking with Gehazi, Elisha's old servant, asking him, 'Tell me some of the crazy miracles Elisha did.'
8.5: And just as Gehazi was telling the king about how Elisha brought somebody back to life, the woman walked in, asking for her land back. Gehazi was like, 'My king, speak of the devil—this the woman right here! And that's her son Elisha brought back to life!'
8.6: The king asked her about it, and she confirmed everything. So he appointed an officer and told him, 'Give her back everything she lost—including all the money her land made while she was gone.'
8.7: Elisha went to Damascus, where Ben-Hadad, the king of Syria, was sick. Word got around that the man of God was in town.
8.8: So the king told Hazael, 'Take some gifts and go ask Elisha if I'm gonna recover from this sickness.'
8.9: Hazael packed up all kinds of stuff—forty camel-loads worth of gifts—and went to Elisha. He said, 'Your boy Ben-Hadad, king of Syria, sent me to ask if he gonna make it.'
8.10: Elisha said, 'Go ahead and tell him he'll recover, but in reality, the Lord showed me he gonna die.'
8.11: Elisha just stared at Hazael for a while, until Hazael started feeling uncomfortable. Then Elisha started crying.
8.12: Hazael was like, 'Why you crying, man?' Elisha said, 'Because I know the evil you about to do to Israel—burning cities, killing young men, smashing babies, and ripping open pregnant women.'
8.13: Hazael was like, 'What? Me? I ain't nobody important. How I'm supposed to do all that?' Elisha said, 'The Lord showed me—you gon' be king of Syria.'
8.14: Hazael left and went back to Ben-Hadad. The king asked, 'What Elisha say?' Hazael said, 'Oh, he said you gon' be alright.'
8.15: But the next day, Hazael took a thick cloth, soaked it in water, and smothered Ben-Hadad till he died. Then Hazael took the throne.
8.16: Back in Judah, during the fifth year of Joram (Ahab's son) ruling over Israel, Jehoshaphat's son Jehoram became king of Judah.
8.17: He was 32 years old when he took the throne, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eight years.
8.18: But he was out here wildin' like the kings of Israel, 'cause he married Ahab's daughter. He was doing evil just like the rest of Ahab's family.
8.19: Even so, the Lord didn't wipe Judah out, 'cause He made a promise to David to keep his family line going forever.
8.20: During Jehoram's reign, Edom got tired of being under Judah and set up their own king.
8.21: So Jehoram rolled up with his chariots, attacked them at night, and tried to hold them down—but his army ended up running back home.
8.22: And from that day forward, Edom stayed independent from Judah. Around the same time, Libnah also broke free.
8.23: Everything else Jehoram did? It's written in the chronicles of the kings of Judah.
8.24: Then Jehoram died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Ahaziah took over after him.
8.25: In the twelfth year of Joram (Ahab's son) ruling Israel, Jehoram's son Ahaziah became king of Judah.
8.26: Ahaziah was 22 years old when he started ruling, but he only lasted one year in Jerusalem. His mama was Athaliah, granddaughter of Omri, king of Israel.
8.27: Ahaziah followed the same wicked ways as Ahab's family, since he was connected to them by marriage. He did evil just like them.
8.28: Ahaziah teamed up with Joram, Ahab's son, to fight against Hazael, the king of Syria, at Ramoth Gilead. But the Syrians injured Joram in battle.
8.29: Joram went back to Jezreel to heal from his wounds, and Ahaziah went down to visit him since he was hurt.

9.1: Elisha called up one of his young prophets and said, 'Get ready, grab this oil, and go to Ramoth Gilead.'
9.2: 'When you get there, find Jehu—son of Jehoshaphat, grandson of Nimshi. Pull him aside from his crew and take him to a private room.'
9.3: 'Then pour this oil on his head and tell him, "The Lord says: I anoint you king over Israel." After that, open the door and run—don't stick around!'
9.4: So the young prophet went to Ramoth Gilead.
9.5: When he got there, the army officers were chilling. He said, 'Commander, I got a word for you.' Jehu said, 'Which one of us?' The prophet said, 'You, Commander.'
9.6: So Jehu got up, went inside, and the prophet poured the oil on his head, saying, 'The Lord says: I'm making you king over Israel.'
9.7: 'You gotta wipe out Ahab's whole house to avenge the blood of my servants and prophets that Jezebel killed.'
9.8: 'Ahab's whole family getting cut off—slave and free, don't matter.'
9.9: 'His house finna be just like Jeroboam's and Baasha's—wiped out.'
9.10: 'And Jezebel? Dogs gon' eat her body in Jezreel, and nobody gon' bury her.' Then the prophet opened the door and ran off.
9.11: Jehu came back out, and his people asked, 'Bruh, what did that crazy dude want?' Jehu said, 'Y'all know how prophets talk.'
9.12: They said, 'Stop playing, tell us the truth!' So Jehu said, 'He told me the Lord said, "I anoint you king over Israel."'
9.13: Right then, they took their cloaks, laid them on the steps for Jehu, blew their trumpets, and shouted, 'Jehu is king!'
9.14: So Jehu started plotting against Joram. Now Joram had been at Ramoth Gilead, defending Israel against Hazael, king of Syria.
9.15: But he got wounded and went to Jezreel to recover. Jehu told his people, 'If y'all with me, don't let anybody leave the city to warn Jezreel.'
9.16: Then Jehu hopped in his chariot and headed straight for Jezreel, where Joram was recovering. Ahaziah, king of Judah, was also there visiting Joram.
9.17: A watchman on the tower in Jezreel saw Jehu's squad coming and told Joram. Joram said, 'Send a rider to ask if it's peace.'
9.18: The rider went out and asked, 'The king says: Is everything good?' Jehu said, 'What you worried about peace for? Fall in behind me.' The watchman reported, 'He met them, but he ain't coming back.'
9.19: Joram sent another rider. Same thing happened—he didn't come back.
9.20: The watchman said, 'Yo, this driving look wild—it gotta be Jehu. He drives crazy!'
9.21: Joram said, 'Get my chariot ready.' He and Ahaziah rode out to meet Jehu at Naboth's old field.
9.22: Joram asked, 'Jehu, we good?' Jehu said, 'Ain't no peace while your mama Jezebel out here with all her witchcraft and mess.'
9.23: Joram turned his chariot to run and yelled, 'Ahaziah, it's a setup!'
9.24: Jehu pulled his bow back full strength and shot Joram in the back—the arrow went straight through his heart. He collapsed in his chariot.
9.25: Jehu told his captain, 'Throw his body in Naboth's field. Remember how we was with Ahab when God said he'd pay him back for what he did to Naboth?'
9.26: 'Well, here's that payback. Toss him in that field, just like God said.'
9.27: Ahaziah saw this and took off toward Beth-Haggan. Jehu said, 'Shoot him too!' They hit him near Gur, but he kept running till he reached Megiddo, where he died.
9.28: His servants took him back to Jerusalem and buried him with his ancestors in the City of David.
9.29: Ahaziah had become king of Judah in Joram's eleventh year of ruling Israel.
9.30: When Jehu pulled up in Jezreel, Jezebel heard about it. She did her makeup, fixed her hair, and looked out the window.
9.31: When Jehu came through the gate, she said, 'So you coming in peace, Zimri? You know, the one who killed his master?'
9.32: Jehu looked up at the window and said, 'Who rolling with me?' Two or three eunuchs looked out.
9.33: Jehu said, 'Throw her down.' And they did. Her blood splattered on the wall, on the horses, and Jehu ran over her with his chariot.
9.34: Jehu went inside, ate, drank, then said, 'Alright, go bury her. She was a king's daughter.'
9.35: But when they went out to bury her, all they found was her skull, feet, and hands.
9.36: They came back and told Jehu, and he said, 'Welp, guess that's just like what Elijah prophesied—dogs ate Jezebel in Jezreel.'
9.37: 'Now she ain't even got a proper grave—just some scraps left in the dirt, like trash.'

10.1: Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. Jehu wrote letters and sent them to the leaders in Jezreel, the elders, and the folks raising Ahab's sons.
10.2: 'Y'all got chariots, horses, weapons, and a whole fortified city. Pick the best son of Ahab, put him on the throne, and fight for his family.'
10.3: But they got shook and said, 'Man, two kings couldn't stand up to Jehu. What we supposed to do?'
10.4: So the palace manager, city officials, elders, and the guardians of Ahab's sons sent Jehu a message: 'We your servants. We'll do whatever you say, but we ain't making anybody king. Just tell us what you want.'
10.5: Jehu sent another letter: 'If y'all really with me, take the heads of Ahab's sons and bring them to me in Jezreel by this time tomorrow.'
10.6: Now Ahab's seventy sons were being raised by the city's leaders, so when they got Jehu's message, they took all seventy, killed them, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to Jezreel.
10.7: A messenger came to Jehu and said, 'Boss, they brought the heads.' Jehu said, 'Pile them up at the city gate 'til morning.'
10.8: The next morning, Jehu went out and said to the people, 'Y'all see this? Yeah, I took out my master, but who killed all these?'
10.9: 'Now y'all know—everything the Lord said about Ahab's house is coming true. This is exactly what He promised through Elijah.'
10.10: Then Jehu wiped out everybody left from Ahab's house in Jezreel—his officials, friends, and priests—nobody was spared.
10.11: Jehu left for Samaria. On the way, he stopped at Beth Eked of the Shepherds.
10.12: There, he ran into the relatives of Ahaziah, king of Judah. He asked, 'Who y'all?'
10.13: They said, 'We Ahaziah's brothers. We just came to visit the king's sons and the queen mother's family.'
10.14: Jehu said, 'Take them alive!' They grabbed all forty-two men and killed them at the well of Beth Eked. None survived.
10.15: As Jehu was leaving, he ran into Jehonadab, son of Rechab. Jehu greeted him and asked, 'You down with me like I'm down with you?'
10.16: Jehonadab said, 'Yeah, I'm with you.' Jehu said, 'Then come with me. See how serious I am about the Lord.' So he got in Jehu's chariot.
10.17: When they got to Samaria, Jehu killed off the rest of Ahab's family—every last one of them—just like the Lord said through Elijah.
10.18: Then Jehu gathered everybody and said, 'Ahab served Baal a little, but me? I'ma take it to another level.'
10.19: 'So go call every Baal prophet, priest, and follower. I got a big sacrifice planned for Baal. If you miss it, you ain't living.' But Jehu was finessing—he was really setting them up.
10.20: He ordered, 'Announce a special service for Baal.' And they did.
10.21: Jehu sent word across Israel, and every single Baal worshiper showed up. The temple was packed.
10.22: He told the temple manager, 'Bring out the special robes for Baal's people.' And they handed them out.
10.23: Then Jehu and Jehonadab went into the temple and said, 'Make sure ain't no servants of the Lord in here—only Baal's people.'
10.24: Once the sacrifices started, Jehu had eighty men waiting outside. He told them, 'If y'all let even one person escape, your life for theirs.'
10.25: As soon as the offering was done, Jehu said, 'Lock the doors. Kill them all.' His men rushed in, took them out with swords, and tossed the bodies outside.
10.26: Then they went into the inner temple, pulled down the sacred pillars, and burned them.
10.27: They tore down Baal's temple and turned it into a garbage dump. It's been like that ever since.
10.28: And that's how Jehu wiped Baal worship out of Israel.
10.29: But even after all that, Jehu still kept the golden calf idols in Bethel and Dan—the same ones Jeroboam set up that led Israel into sin.
10.30: The Lord told Jehu, 'You did good wiping out Ahab's house like I wanted, so your family will rule Israel for four generations.'
10.31: But Jehu didn't fully follow the Lord. He still let Israel run wild in Jeroboam's sins.
10.32: Around this time, the Lord started taking pieces of Israel away, and King Hazael of Syria took over a bunch of land.
10.33: From the Jordan eastward—Gilead, Gad, Reuben, Manasseh—he took it all, from Aroer to Bashan.
10.34: Everything else Jehu did—his victories, his battles—it's all written in the book of the kings of Israel.
10.35: Then Jehu died and was buried in Samaria. His son Jehoahaz took over the throne.
10.36: Jehu ruled Israel from Samaria for twenty-eight years.

11.1: When Athaliah, Ahaziah's mama, saw her son was dead, she went full villain mode and started wiping out the whole royal family.
11.2: But Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram and Ahaziah's sister, wasn't having it. She snatched up Joash, Ahaziah's baby boy, and hid him with his nurse in a bedroom so Athaliah couldn't find him.
11.3: She kept him hidden in the Lord's temple for six years while Athaliah ran the kingdom.
11.4: In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest called up the military captains, the royal guards, and the temple security. He brought them into the temple, made them swear an oath, then showed them the king's son.
11.5: He gave them orders: 'Alright, one-third of y'all guard the king's house.'
11.6: 'Another third, y'all post up at the Gate of Sur. The last third, hold down the gate behind the escorts. Don't let nobody through.'
11.7: 'The rest of y'all, the ones off duty on the Sabbath? Y'all staying in the Lord's house, keeping guard over the king.'
11.8: 'Surround the king from all sides, weapons ready. If anybody tries to come at him—take them out. Stay close to the king when he moves.'
11.9: The captains did exactly what Jehoiada told them. They brought their men on and off duty and met up at the temple.
11.10: Jehoiada handed out weapons—shields and spears from King David's old stash in the temple.
11.11: The guards lined up, fully armed, from one side of the temple to the other, surrounding the king.
11.12: Then they brought Joash out, put the crown on him, gave him the royal scroll, and anointed him king. Everybody started clapping, shouting, 'Long live the king!'
11.13: Athaliah heard all the noise from the temple, so she pulled up to see what was going on.
11.14: She looked and saw the new king standing by the pillar, just like tradition. The officials and trumpeters were celebrating, and the people were hype. Athaliah lost it, tore her clothes, and screamed, 'Treason! Treason!'
11.15: Jehoiada, keeping it cool, told the military captains, 'Get her outta here and handle anybody who tries to back her up.' He made sure they didn't kill her in the Lord's temple.
11.16: So they grabbed her, dragged her through the Horse Gate to the palace, and that's where they took her out.
11.17: Then Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord, the king, and the people, making sure everybody was locked in to serving the Lord.
11.18: Then the people rushed Baal's temple, tore it down, smashed the altars, broke up all the idols, and killed Baal's priest, Mattan, right there at the altar. Jehoiada put new officers in charge of the Lord's house.
11.19: Jehoiada, the military captains, the royal guards, and all the people led Joash from the Lord's house to the palace. He walked through the escort gate and sat on the throne.
11.20: The people cheered, the city calmed down, and just like that—Athaliah was gone.
11.21: Joash was only seven years old when he became king.

12.1: In Jehu's seventh year as king, Jehoash became king of Judah. He ruled for forty years in Jerusalem. His mama was Zibiah from Beersheba.
12.2: Jehoash did right by the Lord as long as Jehoiada the priest was guiding him.
12.3: But one problem—he ain't take down the high places. Folks was still out here burning incense and making sacrifices up there instead of at the Lord's temple.
12.4: One day, Jehoash told the priests, 'Listen, all the money coming into the temple—the census tax, donations, and whatever folks give from their heart—'
12.5: 'Y'all take that and use it to fix up the temple wherever it's falling apart.'
12.6: But fast forward to Jehoash's twenty-third year as king—the priests still ain't fix the temple.
12.7: So Jehoash called Jehoiada and the other priests and said, 'Why y'all ain't done the repairs yet? From now on, stop collecting money for yourselves. Use it to fix the temple like I said.'
12.8: The priests agreed—they would stop collecting money, and they wouldn't be in charge of the repairs anymore.
12.9: Then Jehoiada the priest got a chest, drilled a hole in the top, and put it by the altar, near the entrance of the Lord's house. Every time someone brought money to the temple, the priests put it in the chest.
12.10: When the chest got full, the king's scribe and the high priest would come, bag up the money, and count it.
12.11: They gave the money to the overseers, who then paid the workers—carpenters, builders, masons, stonecutters—anybody fixing up the Lord's house.
12.12: They used the money for materials too—wood, cut stone, and everything needed to restore the temple.
12.13: But none of that money went toward making silver bowls, lamp trimmers, sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or any other gold and silver items for the temple.
12.14: It all went straight to the workers to get the temple repairs done.
12.15: They ain't even make the workers give receipts—everybody handling the money was solid and trustworthy.
12.16: However, the money from guilt offerings and sin offerings wasn't put in the chest—that was strictly for the priests.
12.17: Then Hazael, king of Syria, rolled up on Gath, took the city, and then set his sights on Jerusalem.
12.18: Jehoash, instead of fighting, took all the holy things dedicated by past kings—Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah—plus his own, and all the gold from the temple and the royal treasury. He sent it as a payoff to Hazael, and Hazael left Jerusalem alone.
12.19: Everything else Joash did? It's all written in the book of the kings of Judah.
12.20: But in the end, some of his own servants plotted against him and assassinated him at the house of Millo on the way to Silla.
12.21: The ones who killed him were Jozachar, son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad, son of Shomer. Joash died, they buried him in the City of David, and his son Amaziah took over as king.

13.1: In the twenty-third year of Joash, king of Judah, Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for seventeen years.
13.2: But he was out here wildin'—doing evil just like Jeroboam, who led Israel into sin. He ain't change a thing.
13.3: So the Lord got fed up and let Hazael, king of Syria, and his son Ben-Hadad keep Israel under their thumb for years.
13.4: Eventually, Jehoahaz begged the Lord for help, and the Lord listened, 'cause He saw how bad Israel was suffering under Syria.
13.5: So the Lord sent a deliverer who helped Israel escape Syria's grip. They started living in their own homes again, just like before.
13.6: But even after all that, they still ain't clean up their act. They kept following Jeroboam's ways and even left that wooden idol standing in Samaria.
13.7: By the time Jehoahaz was done, his army was almost wiped out—just fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers left. The king of Syria had crushed them like dust.
13.8: Everything else Jehoahaz did? It's written in the book of the kings of Israel.
13.9: Then he died, they buried him in Samaria, and his son Joash took over.
13.10: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash, king of Judah, Jehoash, son of Jehoahaz, became king of Israel. He ruled in Samaria for sixteen years.
13.11: But he was no better—same old evil, same sins as Jeroboam, keeping Israel on the wrong path.
13.12: Everything else Joash did—including his beef with Amaziah, king of Judah—it's all written in the book of the kings of Israel.
13.13: Then Joash died, was buried in Samaria with the other kings, and his son Jeroboam took the throne.
13.14: Elisha got sick with the illness that would take him out. King Joash of Israel came to see him, crying, 'My father, my father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!'
13.15: Elisha told him, 'Grab a bow and some arrows.' So Joash did.
13.16: 'Now, put your hand on the bow,' Elisha said. Joash did, and Elisha put his hands over the king's hands.
13.17: 'Open the east window,' Elisha said, and Joash opened it. Then Elisha said, 'Shoot!' Joash let the arrow fly. Elisha said, 'That's the Lord's arrow of victory! You gon' take down Syria at Aphek until they're done for.'
13.18: Then Elisha said, 'Grab some more arrows and hit the ground.' Joash struck the ground three times, then stopped.
13.19: Elisha got mad. 'Man, you should've hit it five or six times! Then you would've completely destroyed Syria! But now? You only gon' beat them three times.'
13.20: Then Elisha died, and they buried him. The following spring, raiders from Moab invaded the land.
13.21: Some Israelites were burying a man when they spotted the raiders. They panicked and tossed the body into Elisha's tomb. Soon as the body hit Elisha's bones, the man came back to life and stood up!
13.22: Hazael, king of Syria, kept Israel struggling all through Jehoahaz's reign.
13.23: But the Lord, still faithful to His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, had mercy on Israel. He ain't wipe them out or abandon them yet.
13.24: Then Hazael died, and his son Ben-Hadad took over.
13.25: Joash, son of Jehoahaz, went to war against Ben-Hadad and took back the cities Syria had stolen from his father. Three times Joash defeated him and reclaimed Israel's land.

14.1: In the second year of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, ruling Israel, Amaziah, son of Joash, became king of Judah.
14.2: He was 25 when he took the throne, and he ruled in Jerusalem for 29 years. His mama was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.
14.3: Amaziah did what was right in the Lord's eyes, but he wasn't on David's level. He followed in his daddy Joash's footsteps.
14.4: But he ain't take down the high places, so folks were still out here burning incense and making sacrifices in the wrong spots.
14.5: Once Amaziah had solid control over the kingdom, he handled business—he executed the servants who assassinated his father.
14.6: But he didn't kill their kids, 'cause the law of Moses said, 'Parents don't get punished for their kids' sins, and kids don't get punished for their parents' sins—everybody gets judged for their own mess.'
14.7: Amaziah pulled up on Edom, wiped out 10,000 men in the Valley of Salt, took the city of Sela, and renamed it Joktheel—that name still sticks to this day.
14.8: Then Amaziah sent a message to Jehoash, king of Israel: 'Let's run it. Meet me on the battlefield.'
14.9: Jehoash sent a response: 'Listen, a little thistle in Lebanon told a mighty cedar tree, "Give your daughter to my son," but then a wild animal came through and stomped that thistle out.'
14.10: 'Yeah, you beat Edom, and now you feeling yourself. Stay home, man. Don't start something you can't finish, or you and Judah gonna take an L.'
14.11: But Amaziah wasn't listening. So Jehoash, king of Israel, came through, and they met at Beth Shemesh, which belonged to Judah.
14.12: Judah got whooped bad—everybody ran back home.
14.13: Jehoash even captured Amaziah at Beth Shemesh, then went to Jerusalem, broke down 400 cubits of the city wall—from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.
14.14: He ransacked the Lord's temple, cleaned out the royal treasury, took hostages, and then went back to Samaria.
14.15: Everything else Jehoash did—his power, his battle with Amaziah—it's written in the book of the kings of Israel.
14.16: Then Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. His son Jeroboam took the throne.
14.17: Amaziah, son of Joash, king of Judah, lived 15 more years after Jehoash died.
14.18: Everything else Amaziah did is recorded in the book of the kings of Judah.
14.19: But his own people plotted against him in Jerusalem, so he ran to Lachish. They sent men after him, and he was killed there.
14.20: They brought his body back on horses and buried him in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the City of David.
14.21: Then the people of Judah took his son Azariah, who was just 16, and made him king in his place.
14.22: Azariah rebuilt Elath and brought it back under Judah's control after his father was gone.
14.23: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah ruling Judah, Jeroboam, son of Joash, became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for 41 years.
14.24: But he was on the same mess—doing evil, keeping Israel locked in Jeroboam's sins.
14.25: Still, he managed to restore Israel's borders from Hamath to the Dead Sea, just like the Lord had promised through His prophet Jonah, son of Amittai from Gath-Hepher.
14.26: The Lord saw how bad Israel was struggling—everybody was suffering, slave and free, and they had no help.
14.27: But the Lord wasn't ready to erase Israel from the map yet, so He used Jeroboam to keep them afloat.
14.28: Everything else Jeroboam did—his power, his wars, and how he took back Damascus and Hamath for Israel—it's all recorded in the book of the kings of Israel.
14.29: Then Jeroboam died and was buried with the kings of Israel. His son Zechariah took the throne.

15.1: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam, king of Israel, Azariah, son of Amaziah, became king of Judah.
15.2: He was sixteen when he took the throne and ruled for fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mama was Jecholiah from Jerusalem.
15.3: He did right by the Lord, just like his father Amaziah did.
15.4: But just like before, the high places were still up. People were still out here burning incense and making sacrifices where they shouldn't.
15.5: Then the Lord struck Azariah with leprosy, and he had it for the rest of his life. He had to live in isolation, and his son Jotham ran things in his place.
15.6: Everything else Azariah did? It's all written in the book of the kings of Judah.
15.7: Then he died, they buried him in the City of David, and his son Jotham took the throne.
15.8: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah ruling Judah, Zechariah, son of Jeroboam, became king of Israel in Samaria. He only lasted six months.
15.9: And yeah, he did evil just like his ancestors. He kept Israel deep in Jeroboam's sins.
15.10: Then Shallum, son of Jabesh, plotted against him, killed him in public, and took the throne.
15.11: Everything else Zechariah did? It's in the book of the kings of Israel.
15.12: And just like the Lord told Jehu—'Your family will rule for four generations'—that's exactly what happened.
15.13: Shallum, son of Jabesh, became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah (Azariah), king of Judah. He ruled in Samaria for… one whole month.
15.14: Then Menahem, son of Gadi, came up from Tirzah, stormed into Samaria, killed Shallum, and took over.
15.15: Everything else Shallum did? That's in the book of the kings of Israel.
15.16: After that, Menahem went back to Tirzah and attacked Tiphsah. Since they ain't surrender, he destroyed the whole city—and for real, he was ruthless. He even killed all the pregnant women.
15.17: In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's reign, Menahem, son of Gadi, became king of Israel. He ruled for ten years in Samaria.
15.18: But yeah, same story—he did evil, stuck with Jeroboam's sins, and didn't change a thing.
15.19: Then Pul, king of Assyria, came rolling up. Instead of fighting, Menahem gave him a thousand talents of silver to back off and let him keep his throne.
15.20: To get the money, Menahem taxed the rich folks in Israel—every wealthy man had to cough up fifty shekels of silver to pay off Assyria. After that, Pul left.
15.21: Everything else Menahem did? It's in the book of the kings of Israel.
15.22: Then he died, and his son Pekahiah took the throne.
15.23: In the fiftieth year of Azariah ruling Judah, Pekahiah, son of Menahem, became king of Israel in Samaria. He lasted two years.
15.24: And yup, he did evil too—just like Jeroboam, keeping Israel stuck in sin.
15.25: Then one of his own officers, Pekah, son of Remaliah, plotted against him. He rolled up on Pekahiah in the palace, killed him, and took over.
15.26: Everything else Pekahiah did? That's in the book of the kings of Israel.
15.27: In the fifty-second year of Azariah ruling Judah, Pekah, son of Remaliah, took the throne in Israel. He ruled for twenty years in Samaria.
15.28: But just like everybody before him, he did evil and never stepped away from Jeroboam's sins.
15.29: During Pekah's reign, Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria, invaded and took a bunch of cities—Ijon, Abel Beth Maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee—basically, all of Naphtali's land. Then he deported the people to Assyria.
15.30: Then Hoshea, son of Elah, plotted against Pekah, killed him, and took the throne in Jotham's twentieth year ruling Judah.
15.31: Everything else Pekah did? It's in the book of the kings of Israel.
15.32: In the second year of Pekah ruling Israel, Jotham, son of Uzziah (Azariah), became king of Judah.
15.33: He was twenty-five when he took the throne, and he ruled for sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mama was Jerusha, daughter of Zadok.
15.34: He did right by the Lord, just like his father Uzziah did.
15.35: But again, the high places were still up. People kept sacrificing and burning incense there. Jotham did, however, build the Upper Gate of the Lord's house.
15.36: Everything else Jotham did? That's in the book of the kings of Judah.
15.37: During his reign, the Lord let Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, start trouble with Judah.
15.38: Then Jotham died, was buried with his ancestors in the City of David, and his son Ahaz took the throne.

16.1: In the seventeenth year of Pekah, son of Remaliah, ruling Israel, Ahaz, son of Jotham, became king of Judah.
16.2: Ahaz was 20 when he took the throne, and he ruled for 16 years in Jerusalem. But he wasn't on the right path—he ain't do what was right in the Lord's eyes like his ancestor David did.
16.3: Instead, he followed the ways of Israel's kings. He even sacrificed his own son in fire, doing the same wicked stuff as the nations God had kicked out before Israel moved in.
16.4: He was out here burning incense and making sacrifices on the high places, up in the hills, and under every green tree.
16.5: Then Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, rolled up on Jerusalem, ready for war. They surrounded Ahaz but couldn't take him down.
16.6: At the same time, Rezin took over Elath for Syria, kicked out the people of Judah, and now the Edomites live there to this day.
16.7: So Ahaz panicked and sent messengers to Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria, saying, 'I'm your servant, your son—come help me! These kings of Syria and Israel are ganging up on me!'
16.8: Then Ahaz took all the silver and gold from the Lord's temple and the royal palace and sent it as a gift to the king of Assyria.
16.9: Assyria took the money and went to war for him. They attacked Damascus, captured it, took the people as captives to Kir, and killed King Rezin.
16.10: After that, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria. While he was there, he saw an altar he liked.
16.11: So he sent the blueprint back to Urijah the priest, telling him to build one just like it.
16.12: Urijah wasted no time—before Ahaz even got back, the new altar was ready.
16.13: When Ahaz returned, he went straight to the altar, made some offerings, and poured out a drink offering.
16.14: Then he took the bronze altar from the Lord's temple, moved it from its proper place, and put it on the north side of the new altar he made.
16.15: Ahaz told Urijah, 'From now on, this new altar is where we do all the offerings—morning burnt offerings, evening grain offerings, sacrifices for the king and the people, drink offerings—everything. And sprinkle all the blood here. That old bronze altar? I'll use that when I need guidance.'
16.16: And Urijah the priest? He just went along with everything Ahaz told him to do.
16.17: Then King Ahaz stripped the gold panels off the carts, took the lavers off them, and removed the bronze Sea from the oxen it stood on, putting it on a stone pavement instead.
16.18: He also tore down the special Sabbath entrance that had been built in the Lord's temple, along with the royal entrance—just to impress the king of Assyria.
16.19: Everything else Ahaz did? It's all written in the book of the kings of Judah.
16.20: Then Ahaz died, was buried in the City of David, and his son Hezekiah took the throne.

17.1: In the twelfth year of Ahaz ruling Judah, Hoshea, son of Elah, became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for nine years.
17.2: He was on that same evil path, but not as bad as the kings before him.
17.3: Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, rolled up on him, and Hoshea had to start paying tribute money to stay in power.
17.4: But then Assyria found out Hoshea was playing both sides—he sent messages to So, king of Egypt, trying to make a deal and stopped paying tribute to Assyria. So the king of Assyria wasn't having it—he arrested Hoshea and threw him in prison.
17.5: After that, the king of Assyria marched through Israel, laid siege to Samaria, and surrounded it for three years.
17.6: By Hoshea's ninth year as king, Assyria finally took Samaria and exiled Israel, sending them to Halah, the Habor River, and cities in Medea.
17.7: This all happened 'cause Israel kept sinning against the Lord—the same God who pulled them out of Egypt and freed them from Pharaoh. But instead of staying loyal, they started fearing other gods.
17.8: They copied the ways of the nations God had driven out before them, and they followed the corrupt kings of Israel.
17.9: They thought they could do shady stuff in secret, but God saw everything. They built altars everywhere—from small villages to big cities.
17.10: They set up sacred pillars and idol statues on every high hill and under every green tree.
17.11: They burned incense on those altars just like the pagan nations before them—disrespecting God and making Him angry.
17.12: They worshiped idols, even though God had straight-up told them, 'Don't do this!'
17.13: Over and over, the Lord sent prophets and seers, warning Israel and Judah: 'Turn away from your wicked ways! Follow My commandments! Stick to the laws I gave your ancestors!'
17.14: But they were stubborn, just like their ancestors who refused to trust in God.
17.15: They rejected His laws, broke His covenant, ignored His warnings, and chased after idols. They followed the ways of the surrounding nations, even though God told them not to.
17.16: They completely abandoned the Lord's commandments, made two golden calves, built an idol pole, and started worshiping the sun, moon, stars, and all the false gods.
17.17: They even sacrificed their own kids in fire, practiced witchcraft, and got into sorcery—fully selling out to evil, making God furious.
17.18: So the Lord had enough. He wiped Israel off the map, leaving only Judah.
17.19: But even Judah wasn't acting right—they were following the same corrupt ways as Israel.
17.20: So God rejected the whole nation of Israel, let them get attacked, looted, and finally exiled.
17.21: It all started when Israel broke away from the house of David and made Jeroboam king. He led them away from God, setting them up for destruction.
17.22: Israel kept walking in Jeroboam's sins, never turning back.
17.23: So the Lord finally followed through on His warnings. He had Israel taken out of their land and sent to Assyria—where they still are to this day.
17.24: Then the king of Assyria brought in new people—Babylonians, Cuthites, Avvites, Hamathites, and Sepharvites—to settle in Samaria and take Israel's place.
17.25: But at first, they didn't fear the Lord. So God sent lions among them, and the lions started killing people.
17.26: The new settlers freaked out and told the king of Assyria, 'Look, the people you sent here don't know how to worship the God of this land. That's why lions are attacking them!'
17.27: So the king ordered, 'Send back one of the Israelite priests we captured. Let him teach them how to worship the God of this land.'
17.28: So a priest came back, settled in Bethel, and started teaching them the ways of the Lord.
17.29: But even with that, every group still kept worshiping their own gods, setting up idols in the high places across Samaria.
17.30: The Babylonians made Succoth Benoth. The Cuthites made Nergal. The Hamathites made Ashima.
17.31: The Avvites worshiped Nibhaz and Tartak. And the Sepharvites went as far as burning their kids in fire as sacrifices to Adrammelech and Anammelech, their gods.
17.32: Yeah, they feared the Lord, but at the same time, they still appointed their own priests to serve at the shrines in high places.
17.33: Basically, they were double-dipping—they claimed to respect the Lord but kept serving their own gods, doing things like the nations before them.
17.34: And to this day, they still stuck in their old ways. They don't really fear the Lord or follow His laws and commandments—the same ones He gave Jacob, whom He named Israel.
17.35: God made a covenant with them, saying, 'Don't fear other gods, don't bow down to them, don't serve them, and don't sacrifice to them.'
17.36: 'Fear the Lord—the One who brought you out of Egypt with power. Worship Him and offer sacrifices only to Him.'
17.37: 'Follow His laws, commands, and rules forever. Don't fear other gods.'
17.38: 'And don't forget this covenant I made with y'all. Stick with the Lord, and He'll protect you from your enemies.'
17.39: But they ain't listen. They just kept doing things their own way.
17.40: So, even though they feared the Lord, they still followed their old idolatrous ways.
17.41: And to this very day, their descendants keep doing what their ancestors did—trying to mix worshiping the Lord with serving idols.

18.1: In the third year of Hoshea, son of Elah, ruling over Israel, Hezekiah, son of Ahaz, became king of Judah.
18.2: He was 25 when he took the throne, and he ruled for 29 years in Jerusalem. His mama was Abi, daughter of Zechariah.
18.3: Hezekiah did right by the Lord, following the ways of his ancestor David.
18.4: He tore down all the high places, smashed the sacred pillars, cut down the idol poles, and even destroyed that old bronze snake Moses made—'cause folks had started worshiping it like an idol and calling it Nehushtan.
18.5: Hezekiah trusted in the Lord like no other king before or after him.
18.6: He stayed locked in with the Lord, never straying from His commandments.
18.7: Because of that, the Lord had his back—Hezekiah succeeded in everything he did. He even broke free from the king of Assyria and refused to serve him.
18.8: He pulled up on the Philistines, crushed them all the way to Gaza, taking out both small villages and fortified cities.
18.9: In Hezekiah's fourth year as king—this was Hoshea's seventh year ruling Israel—Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, came for Samaria and laid siege to it.
18.10: Three years later, in Hezekiah's sixth year, Assyria finally took Samaria.
18.11: The king of Assyria deported Israel, sending them off to Halah, the Habor River, and cities in Medea.
18.12: This happened 'cause Israel ain't listen to the Lord. They broke His covenant, ignored Moses' laws, and refused to obey.
18.13: Fast forward to Hezekiah's fourteenth year—Sennacherib, king of Assyria, came through and took over all the fortified cities of Judah.
18.14: Hezekiah sent word to the king of Assyria at Lachish: 'My bad. I messed up. Just tell me what you want, and I'll pay up.' Sennacherib demanded 300 talents of silver and 30 talents of gold.
18.15: So Hezekiah emptied out all the silver from the Lord's temple and the royal treasury.
18.16: He even stripped the gold off the temple doors and pillars that he himself had covered in gold—and sent it all to the king of Assyria.
18.17: Then the king of Assyria sent his top officials—the Tartan, the Rabsaris, and the Rabshakeh—with a huge army to Jerusalem. They pulled up to the aqueduct by the highway leading to the Fuller's Field.
18.18: When they got there, they called for the king. Hezekiah's team—Eliakim (palace overseer), Shebna (the scribe), and Joah (the recorder)—came out to meet them.
18.19: The Rabshakeh said, 'Tell Hezekiah: The great king of Assyria got a question—why you acting so bold?'
18.20: 'You talking like you got some kind of military strategy, but that's just talk. Who you really trusting in that got you thinking you can rebel against me?'
18.21: 'Oh, I see. You putting your faith in Egypt? Man, Egypt is like a broken stick—lean on them, and they'll stab you in the hand. That's Pharaoh for you!'
18.22: 'Or maybe you saying, "We trust in the Lord." Ain't Hezekiah the same one who tore down all those altars and said y'all could only worship in Jerusalem?'
18.23: 'Tell you what—make a deal with my master, the king of Assyria. I'll even give you 2,000 horses… if y'all got enough riders to put on them!'
18.24: 'You can't even take on my lowest-ranking officer, but you think Egypt's chariots and horsemen gon' save you?'
18.25: 'Matter of fact, you think I'm here on my own? The Lord Himself told me to come destroy this place!'
18.26: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, 'Yo, can you speak in Aramaic? We understand it. No need to talk in Hebrew where everybody can hear.'
18.27: But the Rabshakeh laughed and said, 'Nah, I'm talking to everybody—y'all and the people sitting on the walls who about to suffer, starving and drinking their own waste.'
18.28: Then he stepped forward and shouted in Hebrew, 'Listen up, everybody! Hear what the great king of Assyria has to say!'
18.29: 'Don't let Hezekiah fool you—he can't save you!'
18.30: 'Don't let him trick you into trusting the Lord, saying, "The Lord will deliver us, and we won't fall to the king of Assyria."'
18.31: 'Here's what you should do—make peace with me, bring me a gift, and come out. Then every one of y'all can eat from your own vine, drink from your own well, and live good.'
18.32: 'Soon enough, I'll take you to a new land, just like yours—good food, vineyards, olive trees, and honey. You'll live, not die! But don't listen to Hezekiah when he tells you, "The Lord will save us."'
18.33: 'Ain't no god ever saved their people from me! Not Hamath, not Arpad, not Sepharvaim, Hena, or Ivah!'
18.34: 'Even Samaria fell to me! What makes y'all think your God gon' save Jerusalem?'
18.35: The people ain't say a word, 'cause Hezekiah had already told them, 'Don't respond.'
18.36: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah went back to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him everything the Rabshakeh said.
18.37: Then Eliakim (son of Hilkiah, the palace overseer), Shebna (the scribe), and Joah (son of Asaph, the recorder) went back to Hezekiah, clothes ripped in grief, and told him everything the Rabshakeh had said.

19.1: When King Hezekiah heard all this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went straight to the Lord's temple.
19.2: Then he sent Eliakim (his chief of staff), Shebna (his scribe), and the senior priests—all dressed in sackcloth—to go see the prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz.
19.3: They told Isaiah, 'Hezekiah says today is a straight-up disaster—like a woman in labor who ain't got the strength to push.'
19.4: 'Maybe the Lord heard all that trash talk from the Rabshakeh—how he was sent by the Assyrian king to diss the living God. Maybe the Lord will put him in check. So please, pray for the small remnant that's left.'
19.5: When Hezekiah's officials got to Isaiah,
19.6: Isaiah told them, 'Go tell your king this is what the Lord says: "Don't trip over what you just heard—all that mess from Assyria's men blaspheming Me."'
19.7: 'I'm about to send a spirit to stir things up—he's gonna hear a rumor, run back to his own land, and get taken out with the sword over there.'
19.8: Meanwhile, the Rabshakeh got word that his king was fighting in Libnah, 'cause he had left Lachish.
19.9: Then Assyria's king heard that Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia, was coming for him. So he sent another message to Hezekiah:
19.10: 'Tell Hezekiah, king of Judah: Don't let that God you believe in fool you into thinking Jerusalem won't fall into my hands.'
19.11: 'You heard what me and my ancestors did to all those other nations—completely wiped 'em out. You think you're the exception?'
19.12: 'Where were the gods of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, or Eden in Telassar? They couldn't stop us.'
19.13: 'Where's the king of Hamath? The king of Arpad? The kings of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? Gone.'
19.14: When Hezekiah got the letter, he read it, then went straight to the temple, spread it out before the Lord, and prayed.
19.15: Hezekiah said, 'Lord, God of Israel, You sit between the cherubim. You alone are God over every kingdom on earth. You made heaven and earth.'
19.16: 'Open Your ears, Lord—hear this. Open Your eyes, Lord—see what's happening. Listen to what Sennacherib is saying about You, the living God.'
19.17: 'Yeah, it's true—the Assyrians wiped out those nations.'
19.18: 'But their gods weren't real. Just wood and stone, made by human hands. Of course they burned them.'
19.19: 'But now, Lord our God, I'm asking You—save us from this man. Show all the kingdoms of the earth that You alone are God.'
19.20: Then Isaiah, son of Amoz, sent this message to Hezekiah: 'The Lord says: Because you prayed about Sennacherib, king of Assyria, I heard you.'
19.23: 'You really thought you could insult the Holy One of Israel?'
19.24: 'You bragged about climbing mountains, cutting down mighty trees, and drinking foreign waters like you run the world.'
19.25: 'But did you not know? I planned this long ago! You only did what I allowed—turning strong cities into rubble.'
19.26: 'That's why their people were weak—like grass in the field, barely growing before they got stomped out.'
19.27: 'I know where you live. I see what you do. And I know your arrogance against Me.'
19.28: 'Because you raged against Me, your pride has reached My ears. So guess what? I'm putting My hook in your nose, My bridle in your mouth, and sending you right back the way you came.'
19.29: 'And here's a sign for Judah: This year, you'll eat what grows naturally. Next year, same thing. But in the third year, you'll plant and harvest, grow vineyards, and feast.'
19.30: 'The remnant left in Judah will take root and flourish.'
19.31: 'Because from Jerusalem, a remnant will rise again. The zeal of the Lord will make it happen.'
19.32: 'As for the king of Assyria? He won't step foot in this city. He won't even shoot an arrow here.'
19.33: 'The same road he came on, he's leaving on. He's not touching this city.'
19.34: 'Because I, the Lord, will defend it—for My own sake and for My servant David's sake.'
19.35: That night, the angel of the Lord went into the Assyrian camp and wiped out 185,000 soldiers. The next morning, the survivors woke up to nothing but dead bodies.
19.36: So Sennacherib, king of Assyria, packed up and went back home to Nineveh.
19.37: While he was worshiping in the temple of his god, Nisroch, his own sons—Adrammelech and Sharezer—snuck up and killed him with a sword. Then they escaped to Ararat, and Esarhaddon, his son, took over the throne.

20.1: Around that time, Hezekiah got real sick—like, on his deathbed. The prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz, came to him and said, 'The Lord says: Get your affairs in order. You about to die, you ain't gon' make it.'
20.2: Hezekiah turned to the wall and started praying hard to the Lord.
20.3: 'Lord, please remember how I been walking in Your truth with a loyal heart, doing right in Your eyes.' Then Hezekiah broke down crying.
20.4: Before Isaiah even made it out the palace, the Lord hit him with another message.
20.5: 'Go back and tell Hezekiah, the leader of My people: The Lord, the God of David, your ancestor, says—"I heard your prayer, I saw your tears. I got you. You gon' be healed. In three days, you'll be back at My temple."'
20.6: 'I'm adding 15 more years to your life. And on top of that, I'm saving you and this city from the king of Assyria. I'll defend this place for My sake and for David's sake.'
20.7: Then Isaiah said, 'Get a lump of figs.' They brought it, put it on Hezekiah's boil, and just like that, he got better.
20.8: Hezekiah asked Isaiah, 'What sign is the Lord gon' give me to prove I'll be healed and back in the temple in three days?'
20.9: Isaiah said, 'Alright, this is the sign from the Lord—do you want the shadow on the sundial to move forward ten steps or back ten steps?'
20.10: Hezekiah said, 'Man, it's too easy for the shadow to go forward. Make it go back ten steps instead.'
20.11: So Isaiah prayed, and the Lord made the shadow move back ten steps on the sundial of Ahaz.
20.12: Later, Berodach-Baladan, son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent Hezekiah letters and a gift 'cause he heard Hezekiah had been sick.
20.13: Hezekiah welcomed them in and started showing off—gave them a full tour of his treasure house: all the silver, gold, spices, fine oils, his entire armory—everything. He left nothing out.
20.14: Then Isaiah came to Hezekiah and asked, 'Who were those men? Where they from?'
20.15: Hezekiah said, 'They came from Babylon—a faraway place.'
20.16: Isaiah asked, 'What all did they see?' Hezekiah said, 'Everything. I showed them all my treasures. I didn't hold back anything.'
20.17: Then Isaiah hit him with a word from the Lord: 'Listen up—days are coming when everything in your palace, all the wealth your ancestors stored up, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left.'
20.18: 'Even some of your own sons—your descendants—gon' be taken as captives, made into eunuchs in the king of Babylon's palace.'
20.19: Hezekiah said, 'Well… at least the Lord's word is good.' He was thinking, 'At least things gon' stay peaceful while I'm still alive.'
20.20: Everything else Hezekiah did—all his power, how he built the water tunnel to bring water into the city—it's all written in the book of the kings of Judah.
20.21: Then Hezekiah died and was buried with his ancestors. His son Manasseh took over the throne.

21.1: Manasseh was just 12 years old when he became king, and he ruled for 55 years in Jerusalem. His mama was Hephzibah.
21.2: But he was wild—he did evil just like the nations God kicked out before Israel moved in.
21.3: He brought back all the high places his daddy Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for Baal, made an Asherah pole like Ahab had done, and started worshiping the sun, moon, and stars.
21.4: On top of that, he built altars inside the Lord's own temple—the place where God had said, 'This is My spot in Jerusalem.'
21.5: He even put altars for the stars in both courtyards of the Lord's house.
21.6: And it gets worse—Manasseh sacrificed his own son in fire, got deep into witchcraft, sorcery, fortune-telling, and was consulting psychics and mediums. Straight-up disrespecting the Lord.
21.7: Dude even put a carved idol of Asherah inside the Lord's temple—the same place where God told David and Solomon, 'I chose this city out of all Israel. My name stays here forever.'
21.8: 'I promised I wouldn't kick Israel off their land—as long as they followed My commands, like Moses told them.'
21.9: But Manasseh had them out here acting worse than the nations God had destroyed before them.
21.10: The Lord sent prophets with a message.
21.11: 'Manasseh, king of Judah, has done straight-up evil—worse than even the Amorites before him. And he led Judah into sin too.'
21.12: 'So here's what's coming—Judah and Jerusalem are about to get hit so bad that just hearing about it will make people's ears ring.'
21.13: 'I'm about to judge Jerusalem the same way I did Samaria and Ahab's house. I'm wiping this city clean—like wiping a plate, turning it upside down.'
21.14: 'I'm done with y'all. I'm letting your enemies take over, and y'all gonna be looted and carried off.'
21.15: 'This been a long time coming—Israel been acting up since the day I freed them from Egypt.'
21.16: Manasseh wasn't just leading people into sin—he had innocent people killed left and right, till Jerusalem was soaked in blood from one end to the other.
21.17: Everything else he did? It's in the book of the kings of Judah.
